lead: Recent discussions on climate change highlight critical blind spots in our models and the urgent need for monitoring feedback loops exacerbated by rising temperatures.

stories.title: Our climate models have a big, dangerous blind spot
stories.summary: Climate change is not just a consequence of human activity; it is now driving further climate change through dangerous feedback loops. Current climate models fail to fully account for these dynamics, posing significant risks to our emissions-reduction goals. Scientists warn that without addressing these blind spots, we may underestimate the severity of climate impacts.

stories.title: The Download: AI agent tracking and climate feedback loops
stories.summary: As climate change accelerates, the role of AI in monitoring and managing its effects becomes increasingly vital. Experts argue for the real-time tracking of AI agents to ensure they contribute positively to climate solutions rather than exacerbate the situation. This call for better governance in AI reflects a broader need to integrate technology with environmental stewardship.

stories.title: ‘There is no inevitable dystopia’: Jeanette Winterson on AI and the future of humanity
stories.summary: Author Jeanette Winterson discusses the intersection of AI and climate change, suggesting that humanity stands at a pivotal moment. She emphasizes the importance of storytelling in shaping our future, particularly in addressing the challenges posed by climate change and technology. Winterson's reflections encourage a proactive approach to creating a sustainable future.
